text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- By 2006 Poland's inflation may fall to 2.5 percent, which would enable the country to join the European Monetary Union (EMU), Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said.

- The listed Mostostal Zabrze construction firm will carry out a construction contract for the U.S.'s General Motors worth 17 million marks. Mostostal will participate in GM's new plant construction in Gliwice, southern Poland.
- Turnover of France's Sodexho catering group in 1996 was 5.069 million zlotys but its annual net result was negative, Sodexho Poland president Gilles Poirieux said.

- The annual revenues of the Wroclaw-based PZL Hydral aircraft equipment maker in 1996 reached 100 million zlotys. Thanks to its successful restructuring, the company received an International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9001 certificate for management and product quality in October last year.
NOWA EUROPA

- Four state-owned asbestos tile makers were exempted from the recently introduced ban on asbestos production. The remaining firms have had to stop production and the plants' trade unions are pressing the government to facilitate non-asbestos technologies acquisition.

- Around 190 firms operating in the heavily industrialised Katowice province will be privatised through a regional scheme similar to the National Investment Fund (NFI) programme, experts at the provincial governor's office and the Business Consulting advising firm said.

- A "Little Holland" business and leisure plaza will be built in the northern coastal Zulawy estuary in cooperation with the Polish Dutch friendship society. The project will mirror Dutch infrastractural and architecture patterns.
- Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (BH COK) recommended buying shares of the Elektrobudowa construction firm in its report dated December 6.
- The listed Okocim brewer will develop production facilities to increase output from 1.35 million to 1.65 million hectolitres. Denmark's Carlsberg holds a 32-percent stake in the company.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Almost 40 perecent of Poland's trade turnover in 1996 was made in the fourth quarter, traders said. Perfume sales grew tenfold in mid-December.
- Only 283 flats were constructed in the Opole province last year. To match western standards the province should build 8,000 flats every year, the province's business director Stefan Ksiazek said.

- The Infor publishing firm had a turnover of 60 million zlotys last year and its net profit reached four million zlotys, showing a 100-percent increase compared with the previous year, the firm's president Ryszard Pienkowski said.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- The Kalisz and Konin municipalities have formed a company with the Energetyka Kaliska electricity supplier to cut the costs of energy and improve service standards.
- Poland's smokers prefer low-price high-tar cigarettes produced domestically. Over 60 percent of Poles are smokers, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's Nowy Sacz, Sieradz, Leszno and Krosno provinces will receive a five-million-zloty subsidy from the European agricultural assistance fund to finance road construction in rural areas.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
